text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finnish farmers unhappy about EU bureaucracy.
- Many Norwegians choose Finland for pre-Christmas celebrations since Finnish prices are clearly cheaper.
- The Conservative Party and the Centre Parties are about equal in popularity, new poll shows. Social Democrats still the leading political party.
- Extra tax cuts are political watershed both within the government and the opposition.

- Tuomo Halonen -- about to change its name to Elecster by which it is better known abroad -- has almost tripled its share price this year after an invention that turns waste milk whey into a raw material in making infant food.
- Asko's furniture unit to open interior design store in Estonian capital Tallinn.
- Telcommunications group Nokia could help the Stockholm stock exchange become the central marketplace of the Nordic countries if its turnover there increased.
- DNA studies may help identify young men in risk of sudden heart failure.
- Sex, work and Santa Claus among most used internet search words in Finland, says 'www.fi/top100.html'.
